title: How to hide cursor in Zoom on Mac: simple solutions for clear screen sharing
metaTitle: How to hide cursor in Zoom on Mac
description: Learn how to hide cursor in Zoom on Mac. There is no native setting, so follow these workflows and tools to keep your screen shares clean and professional.
intro: There is no native setting within the Zoom desktop app for macOS to hide your cursor during a live meeting. You must use third party utilities or specific workflow techniques to keep the cursor invisible while sharing your screen.
tldr: Zoom has no built in option to hide your mouse cursor.
Use a third party tool like Cursorcerer to toggle cursor visibility with a hotkey.
Try moving your cursor to the extreme edge of your screen to trigger system hiding.
Join via the web browser version of Zoom to see if it changes capture behavior.
Post production editing is the most reliable way to remove cursors from recorded sessions.

blocks.text: Many presenters want to hide the mouse cursor to keep the focus on their slides or application content. When you share your screen in Zoom on a Mac, the app captures exactly what the operating system sends to the display. Because macOS does not provide a system wide toggle to turn off the cursor, Zoom cannot simply switch it off for you.
Why Zoom cannot hide the cursor natively

Zoom acts as a mirror for your screen. It records or transmits the pixels exactly as they appear on your display. If your cursor is visible to you, it is visible to your audience. Many users look for a setting in the Zoom preferences menu to toggle this off, but it does not exist. The application does not have the necessary permissions to override macOS system level cursor rendering during a live stream.
Using Cursorcerer to hide your mouse cursor

The most effective way to hide your cursor is using a utility that intercepts the cursor at the window server level. Cursorcerer is a popular free tool designed specifically for this task on macOS. It allows you to toggle the cursor visibility using a global hotkey. This works across all applications, including Zoom.

items: Download and install Cursorcerer from the developer website.
Open the app and configure your preferred toggle shortcut.
The default shortcut is usually ⌃ + ⌥ + K.
Before starting your screen share, press the hotkey to hide the cursor.
Press it again when you need to interact with your interface.

blocks.text: The manual move and pause technique

If you cannot install third party software, you can use the manual approach. This requires practice and patience. Move your cursor to the far edge of your screen or into a corner where it will not distract your audience. In some macOS contexts, the system will hide the cursor after a few seconds of inactivity.

items: Complete your click or selection action.
Move the mouse pointer to the extreme corner of your monitor.
Wait for the system to hide the cursor automatically.
Avoid moving the mouse until you absolutely need to click something new.

blocks.text: Joining via web browser as a workaround

Some users find that the Zoom web client treats screen capture differently than the native desktop application. If you have persistent issues with the cursor appearing or behaving erratically, try joining the meeting through your web browser at zoom.us. This method sometimes bypasses specific app level capture behaviors that cause the cursor to remain visible or glitchy.

Sometimes the cursor disappears when you want it to be visible. This is often a sign of a graphics rendering conflict or a configuration issue within macOS. Ensure your Zoom window is on your primary display. If you have multiple monitors, the cursor might be getting lost in the transition between them during the capture process.
Post production editing for recorded sessions

If your primary goal is to have a clean video for a recording, you do not need to hide the cursor during the live session. You can remove it later using video editing software like Screen Studio or OBS Studio. This is often the best approach for professional tutorials or webinars where you need to interact with the screen but do not want the cursor in the final output.
Common mistakes when managing screen visibility

Do not confuse cursor hiding with accessibility settings. Changing your cursor size or color in System Settings > Accessibility > Display > Pointer will not hide it. It will only make it larger or more colorful, which might actually make it more distracting to your meeting participants. Stick to the methods that toggle the visibility layer directly.

faq.question: Can I hide the cursor inside Zoom settings?
faq.answer: No. There is no native setting in the Zoom desktop app to hide your cursor during screen sharing.

faq.question: Does Cursorcerer work on all macOS versions?
faq.answer: Always check the compatibility notes for the latest macOS release like Sequoia or Tahoe on the developer website before installing.

faq.question: Will hiding the cursor affect my ability to click?
faq.answer: Yes. When the cursor is hidden, you will not see where you are pointing. You must remember to toggle it back on when you need to click buttons.

faq.question: Is there a way to hide the cursor only in recordings?
faq.answer: Yes. You can use video editing software like Screen Studio to remove or hide the cursor in post production.

steps.name: Download Cursorcerer
steps.text: Visit the official Cursorcerer website and download the latest version compatible with your macOS.

steps.name: Install the utility
steps.text: Open the downloaded file and move it to your Applications folder, then launch it.

steps.name: Set your hotkey
steps.text: In the Cursorcerer preferences, define a global hotkey to toggle your cursor visibility.

steps.name: Toggle before sharing
steps.text: Before you begin your Zoom screen share, press your chosen hotkey to hide the cursor.

troubleshooting.fix: Check for graphics rendering conflicts or ensure Zoom is on the primary display.
Sign out of all devices at zoom.us/profile and sign back in.
